subject: Computer Networking
title: Smart NICs and DPUs
description: A quick win: understand Smart NICs and DPUs.

hook.text: What if your network card had its own processor? Smart NICs offload work from the CPU to the card.

buildup.text: Traditional NICs just send and receive. Smart NICs — DPUs — filter, encrypt, and route on-card.

discovery.text: Cloud providers use DPUs to isolate tenant traffic in hardware. The server CPU runs only customer work.

twist.text: NVIDIA BlueField and AMD Pensando run a full network OS on a chip smaller than a credit card.

climax.text: Offloading to the DPU frees 10-30% server CPU. In a data center, that translates to billions saved.

punchline.text: Smart NICs do the networking so the CPU doesn't have to.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of a DPU in cloud data centers?
options: It frees the server CPU by offloading network processing to the card
It replaces the need for network cables
It provides wireless connectivity to servers

details.summary: Smart NICs and data processing units offload network, storage, and security functions from server CPUs onto dedicated processors embedded in the network card. They handle encryption, firewalling, load balancing, and storage virtualization, freeing CPU cores entirely for application workloads.
details.whyItMatters: As network speeds reach 100 Gbps and beyond, CPUs cannot keep up with network processing. Smart NICs and DPUs are essential for maintaining performance in modern cloud and data center environments.
takeaways: Smart NICs offload networking tasks from the server CPU
DPUs add programmable processors for security and storage
Cloud providers use DPUs to isolate tenant workloads efficiently

faq.question: What is the difference between a smart NIC and a DPU?
faq.answer: Smart NICs add fixed-function offload engines to a network card for tasks like encryption and checksum. DPUs include fully programmable ARM or RISC-V processors plus network ASICs, enabling complex software-defined networking, security, and storage functions entirely on the card.

faq.question: Why do cloud providers use DPUs?
faq.answer: Cloud providers like AWS run their Nitro system on DPUs to handle virtualization, networking, and storage I/O without consuming any customer CPU cycles. This gives tenants access to the full CPU while the DPU handles all infrastructure overhead invisibly.
